title: Vale of Leven Academy partners with AECOM and NUVIA on pioneering maritime engineering skills programme

body_markdown:
- ***Developed in partnership with Class Of Your Own, initiative forms part of global learning programme***
- ***Initiative will give young people industry-led STEM learning***
- ***Programme will inspire future talent by providing recognised qualifications and insight into engineering careers***


**GLASGOW (November 19, 2026) *—*** Students at Vale of Leven Academy in West Dunbartonshire are set to take part in a pioneering maritime engineering and skills programme developed through a joint partnership between global infrastructure consultancy AECOM, specialist engineering and services company NUVIA, and social enterprise Class Of Your Own.


The Design a Port programme will give students practical experience of planning, designing and presenting a port concept while working towards recognised qualifications. It has been designed to make engineering careers more visible and accessible, including for young people from backgrounds that remain under-represented in the sector, and to support a stronger early talent pipeline into apprenticeships, further education and university.


AECOM and NUVIA, both of which have a strong presence in Scotland, are jointly funding and supporting the programme. Professionals from both organisations will contribute technical insight, mentoring and careers guidance, helping students understand how skills learned in the classroom are applied to complex, real-world infrastructure projects. The partnership will bring together AECOM’s infrastructure and maritime expertise with NUVIA’s expertise in systems thinking, project delivery and safety-led work in highly regulated sectors including nuclear, fusion and defence.


Students aged 13 and over will work in teams to design a small port facility that responds to the needs of the local community and environment. They will consider safety, sustainability, digital engineering and modern methods of construction, and will produce a concept design, digital model, sustainability plan and careers map.


The project will also introduce students to the wider social, environmental and economic role of ports. Using geospatial data and digital twin technology, they will explore factors including topography, tides, water depth, wind, wave patterns and hydrology, as well as how people, goods and vessels can move safely and efficiently through a port environment.


Councillor Michelle McGinty, Convener of Educational Services, West Dunbartonshire Council, said: “This is a fantastic opportunity for our young people to experience STEM in a way that brings learning to life. By working alongside industry professionals on a real-world engineering challenge, pupils at Vale of Leven Academy will develop valuable skills, build confidence and find out more about some of the exciting career opportunities available to them in the future.


“Partnerships like this also help demonstrate to our young people how the knowledge they develop in the classroom can be applied to projects that have a meaningful impact on communities and industries.”


Caroline Smith, Director, AECOM, said: “This is a fantastic initiative that addresses a real industry challenge by helping to develop the skills our sector needs for the future. Through designing their own port facility, students will gain first-hand experience of how STEM subjects are applied in real-world engineering projects and the vital role that ports play in supporting communities and economic growth.


“Our engineers will volunteer their time through our social value programme to work directly with the students, sharing their expertise, providing mentorship and offering a first-hand insight into the opportunities a career in engineering can provide. The initiative is designed to raise awareness of careers in marine engineering and related industries, helping to create a pipeline of skilled professionals for the future. Maritime industries have long been at the heart of many of Scotland’s coastal communities, and developing a strong pipeline of local talent will be vital to supporting their continued growth, innovation and contribution to the country’s economy.”


David Field, Business Director for Defence, NUVIA, said: “We’re delighted to support this initiative. Building the critical capabilities the UK will need for the future starts with giving young people the chance to see where their interest and skills can take them. Design a Port brings learning to life through a real engineering challenge, while opening up routes into technical, vocational and professional careers.


“Our people will share practical experience of safe, complex infrastructure delivery, systems thinking and technical careers, helping students understand both the opportunities and the responsibility that come with engineering. By working with schools and industry partners, we can widen access, develop talent and help create the skilled workforce on which future projects and communities will depend.”


Alison Watson MBE, founder and CEO of Class Of Your Own and creator of Design Engineer Construct!, said: “As a former surveyor with a lifelong passion for the geospatial sector, I am particularly excited to see so many young students exploring the relationship between land and water through this project.


“A successful port begins with a detailed understanding of topography, hydrology, tides, levels and movement. By using geospatial data and digital twin technology, students will be able to investigate a real place, test their decisions and see maths become an essential design tool.


“This is what meaningful built environment education should look like. Students are trusted with a genuine context, teachers are supported by industry, and learning is connected directly to the world beyond the school gates.”


Developed by Class Of Your Own in partnership with AECOM and NUVIA, the new Certified Learning Course forms part of the Design Engineer Construct! (DEC) global learning programme. DEC begins in primary school and progresses into secondary education through a suite of SCQF-recognised qualifications, helping students advance to further and higher education and apprenticeships. Through partnerships with industry and academia, the programme connects STEM learning with real-world applications and introduces students to diverse career pathways across the built environment.


*Students at Vale of Leven Academy in West Dunbartonshire set to take part in a new skills programme by AECOM, NUVIA and Class Of Your Own.*


**About AECOM**


AECOM (NYSE: ACM) is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.


**About NUVIA**


NUVIA is a trusted specialist partner delivering complex projects, engineering, products and services across nuclear, fusion and defence. Backed by VINCI Group, NUVIA works with clients across the full lifecycle of critical programmes, combining technical expertise with a strong focus on safety, people, partnership and accountable delivery. NUVIA is committed to developing talent, creating skilled career pathways and delivering social value in the communities where it works. NUVIA operates across the UK, with a growing presence in Scotland spanning its new Glasgow office and work at nuclear and defence sites, including Faslane and Coulport, Dounreay, Thurso, Hunterston and Chapelcross.


**About Class Of Your Own**


Class Of Your Own (“COYO”) is an award-winning social enterprise founded in 2009 by Alison Watson MBE, creator of the ‘Design Engineer Construct!’ Learning Programme (“DEC”), a pioneering curriculum focusing on the digital Built Environment. By integrating STEM subjects and real-world project-based learning experiences, DEC educates and empowers children and young people to contribute positively to a net zero carbon future, giving them advanced skills and a deep understanding of design, engineering and construction concepts for a more sustainable world.
